items.stem: A random sample of 200 students at a school found that 60 of them prefer online classes. Based on the sample, what is the best estimate of the percent of all students at the school who prefer online classes?
items.explanation: Доля в случайной выборке оценивает долю в генеральной совокупности: 60/200 = 30% (C). 60% — число принято за процент; 6% — сдвиг запятой; 20% — ошибка деления.

items.stem: A survey estimates that 45% of voters support a candidate, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points. Which interval most likely contains the true percent of voters who support the candidate?
items.explanation: Оценка ± погрешность: 45 − 3 = 42, 45 + 3 = 48 (A). B отходит только вверх; C удваивает погрешность; D считает погрешность в долях процента.

items.stem: A researcher wants to estimate the average number of hours of sleep that adults in a city get. Which sampling method is most likely to produce a sample that represents the city's adults?
choices: Selecting adults at random from a list of all adult residents of the city
Surveying people at a gym early in the morning
Surveying the first 50 people who reply to an online post
Surveying the employees of one office
items.explanation: Случайный выбор из списка всех жителей даёт каждому равный шанс попасть в выборку (A). В зале, в соцсетях и в одном офисе выборка смещена: эти люди отличаются от остальных.

items.stem: In a random sample of 50 apples from an orchard, 4 apples were bruised. The orchard has 2,000 apples. Based on the sample, how many apples in the orchard would be expected to be bruised?

In a random sample of adults, the mean height was 165 centimeters, with a margin of error of 2 centimeters. Which of the following is a plausible value for the mean height of all adults in the population?
choices: 164 cm
160 cm
170 cm
168 cm
items.explanation: Правдоподобные значения — от 163 до 167 см. Внутри только 164 (A); 160, 168 и 170 лежат за границами.

items.stem: If all other factors stay the same, what generally happens to the margin of error of a survey when the size of the random sample is increased?
choices: It decreases.
It increases.
It does not change.
It becomes zero.
items.explanation: Чем больше случайная выборка, тем точнее оценка и тем меньше погрешность (A). Нулём она не станет, пока опрашивают не всех (D).

items.stem: In a random sample of 400 voters, 52% said they support a proposal. How many voters in the sample said they support the proposal?
items.explanation: 0.52 · 400 = 208 избирателей.

items.stem: A researcher surveys 500 randomly selected teenagers to estimate the average daily screen time of all teenagers in a country. What is the population in this study?
choices: All teenagers in the country
The 500 teenagers who were surveyed
The researcher's own students
All people in the country
items.explanation: Генеральная совокупность — та группа, о которой делают вывод: все подростки страны (A). 500 опрошенных — выборка (B); D шире, чем нужно.

items.stem: A poll of 1,000 randomly selected adults found that 38% support a policy, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
choices: It is plausible that between 35% and 41% of all adults support the policy.
Exactly 38% of all adults support the policy.
38% of the 1,000 adults will change their minds.
A majority of adults support the policy.
items.explanation: Интервал 38 ± 3 даёт правдоподобные значения 35–41% (A). Точное значение неизвестно (B); C ни о чём не говорит; 41% < 50%, большинства нет (D).

items.stem: A sample mean is 72, and the margin of error is 4.5. What is the upper end of the interval of plausible values for the population mean?
items.explanation: Верхняя граница = оценка + погрешность = 72 + 4.5 = 76.5.

items.stem: To learn about the reading habits of all adults in a town, a researcher surveys shoppers at a bookstore. Why might the results be biased?
choices: Bookstore shoppers are likely to read more than adults in general.
The sample is too random.
The shoppers are adults.
The survey asks about books.
items.explanation: Покупатели книжного читают больше среднего — выборка завышает чтение (A). Случайность выборки — это не причина смещения, а защита от него (B).

items.stem: A random sample of 80 light bulbs of one type had a mean lifetime of 1,200 hours. What is the best estimate of the mean lifetime of all light bulbs of this type?
choices: 1,200 hours
15 hours
96,000 hours
80 hours
items.explanation: Среднее случайной выборки — лучшая оценка среднего совокупности (A). 15 — 1200/80; 96 000 — 1200 · 80 (суммарная наработка); 80 — размер выборки.

items.stem: In a random sample of 120 students at a school, 18 walk to school. The school has 900 students. Based on the sample, about how many students at the school walk to school?
Four random samples are taken from the same population to estimate the same proportion. Which sample size would generally give the smallest margin of error?
items.explanation: Погрешность уменьшается с ростом размера случайной выборки, поэтому наименьшая — у выборки из 1000 (A).

items.stem: Which of the following is a sample statistic?
choices: The mean age of 300 randomly selected residents
The mean age of all residents of a country
The number of people living in the country
A guess about the mean age made before any data are collected
items.explanation: Статистика выборки — число, посчитанное по выборке (A). B — параметр совокупности; C — размер совокупности; D — не результат данных.

items.stem: A random sample of 300 households in a town found a mean of 2.4 cars per household. The town has 12,000 households. Based on the sample, what is the best estimate of the total number of cars owned by households in the town?
items.explanation: Среднее на домохозяйство · число домохозяйств = 2.4 · 12 000 = 28 800 (C). 720 — машины в выборке; 5000 — 12 000/2.4; 36 000 — 3 · 12 000.

items.stem: Survey A used a random sample of 400 people and reported a margin of error of 5 percentage points. Survey B used a random sample of 1,600 people from the same population and reported a margin of error of 2.5 percentage points. Which statement is true?
choices: Survey B's estimate is likely to be closer to the true value because its margin of error is smaller.
Survey A is more precise because its sample is smaller.
The two surveys are equally precise.
Survey B's estimate must be exactly correct.
items.explanation: Меньшая погрешность — более точная оценка (A). Маленькая выборка менее точна (B); точность разная (C); идеальной оценки по выборке не бывает (D).

items.stem: In a random sample of 250 phones from a factory, 15 were defective. Based on the sample, what percent of the factory's phones are expected to be defective?
items.explanation: Доля бракованных в выборке 15/250 = 0.06, то есть 6%.

items.stem: Based on a random sample, an interval of plausible values for the mean commute time of a city's workers is 22 to 30 minutes. What were the sample mean and the margin of error?
choices: Mean 26 minutes, margin of error 4 minutes
Mean 26 minutes, margin of error 8 minutes
Mean 22 minutes, margin of error 8 minutes
Mean 30 minutes, margin of error 4 minutes
items.explanation: Центр интервала (22 + 30)/2 = 26, погрешность — половина ширины: 4 (A). 8 — вся ширина интервала; C и D берут за центр границу.

items.stem: A random sample of 500 residents of a city found that 62% own a bicycle, with a margin of error of 4 percentage points. A newspaper claims that 70% of the city's residents own a bicycle. Is the claim supported by the survey?
choices: No, because 70% is outside the interval from 58% to 66%.
Yes, because 70% is close to 62%.
Yes, because the margin of error is 4%.
No, because the sample size is too large.
items.explanation: Правдоподобные значения 58–66%; 70% за пределами интервала, поэтому опрос утверждение не поддерживает (A). «Близко» — не критерий (B); большая выборка — достоинство, а не недостаток (D).

items.stem: A survey estimates that 47% of customers are satisfied, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points. What is the lower end, in percent, of the interval of plausible values?
items.explanation: Нижняя граница = 47 − 3 = 44%.

items.stem: A survey was mailed to 2,000 randomly selected residents, but only 150 of them returned it. Which is the main concern about using the results to describe all residents?
choices: The residents who responded may differ from those who did not respond.
The residents were selected at random.
2,000 is too many people to survey.
The survey was sent by mail rather than by email.
items.explanation: При низкой доле ответов отвечают чаще те, кому тема важна, — смещение из-за неответов (A). Случайный отбор — плюс (B); размер рассылки не проблема (C).

items.stem: A researcher randomly selects 40 students from each of the 5 high schools in a district and finds that the mean test score of the 200 students is 78. To which group can the result most reasonably be generalized?
choices: Students at the 5 high schools in the district
All high school students in the country
Only the 200 students who took part
Teachers in the district
items.explanation: Выборка случайна только среди учеников этих 5 школ — на них и можно распространить вывод (A). Ученики страны в выборку не попадали (B); C слишком узко — смысл выборки в обобщении.

items.stem: A random sample of 60 cups of coffee from a café had a mean of 95 milligrams of caffeine per cup. The café sells 1,500 cups per week. Based on the sample, estimate the total amount of caffeine, in grams, in the coffee the café sells per week. (1 gram = 1,000 milligrams)

Two polls estimated the percent of voters who support a candidate. Poll 1 reported 48% with a margin of error of 4 percentage points, and poll 2 reported 52% with a margin of error of 4 percentage points. Which statement is true?
choices: The results are consistent with each other because the intervals overlap.
Poll 2 proves that the candidate will win.
Poll 1 must be wrong.
The true percent must be exactly 50%.
items.explanation: Интервалы 44–52% и 48–56% пересекаются, опросы друг другу не противоречат (A). Ни один не доказывает победу (B) и не ошибочен (C); точное значение не известно (D).

items.stem: To estimate the mean weight of fish in a lake, a biologist catches fish with a net that has large holes. Why might the estimate be biased?
choices: Small fish can escape through the holes, so large fish would be overrepresented.
Large fish can escape through the holes, so small fish would be overrepresented.
The lake is too large to sample.
Using a net makes the sample random.
items.explanation: Через крупные ячейки уходит мелкая рыба, поэтому в улове больше крупной и среднее завышено (A). B — наоборот; сеть не делает выборку случайной (D).

items.stem: A sample proportion is 0.36, with a margin of error of 0.05. What is the width of the interval of plausible values for the population proportion?
items.explanation: Интервал от 0.31 до 0.41, ширина — две погрешности: 0.1.

items.stem: A survey of 200 randomly selected people has a margin of error that is too large. Which change would most reduce the margin of error?
choices: Increasing the random sample to 800 people
Surveying only volunteers
Asking more questions in the survey
Surveying only people from one neighborhood
items.explanation: Погрешность уменьшается с ростом случайной выборки (A). Добровольцы и один район вносят смещение; число вопросов на погрешность не влияет.

items.stem: Based on a random sample, the mean number of books read per year by students at a school is estimated to be 9, with a margin of error of 1.5. Which of the following is NOT a plausible value for the mean number of books read by all students at the school?
items.explanation: Правдоподобные значения от 7.5 до 10.5. 11 выходит за границу (A); 8, 10 и 9.5 внутри.

items.stem: In a random sample of 400 people from a population of 25,000, 112 people had a certain trait. Based on the sample, how many people in the population would be expected to have the trait?

A random sample of 1,200 adults estimated that 41% approve of a law, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points. A second random sample of 300 adults from the same population estimated that 46% approve. Which statement about the margin of error for the second sample is most reasonable?
choices: It is likely greater than 3 percentage points.
It is likely less than 3 percentage points.
It must be exactly 3 percentage points.
It is 5 percentage points, the difference between the estimates.
items.explanation: Вторая выборка в 4 раза меньше, поэтому её погрешность больше (примерно вдвое, около 6 пунктов) (A). Разница оценок — не погрешность (D).

items.stem: A survey reported that between 35% and 43% of residents support a proposal, based on a sample percent and a margin of error. What was the sample percent?
items.explanation: Оценка — центр интервала: (35 + 43)/2 = 39%, погрешность 4 пункта.

items.stem: A random sample of employees at a large company shows that employees who work from home report higher job satisfaction than those who work in the office. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
choices: At this company, working from home is associated with higher reported job satisfaction.
Working from home causes higher job satisfaction for all workers.
Every employee who works from home is satisfied with the job.
Higher job satisfaction causes employees to work from home.
items.explanation: Это наблюдение по случайной выборке одной компании: можно говорить о связи и только в этой компании (A). О причине без эксперимента судить нельзя (B, D); о каждом сотруднике — тоже (C).

items.stem: A random sample of 100 people gives a margin of error of 10 percentage points. Assume the margin of error is proportional to 1/√n, where n is the sample size. About what sample size is needed for a margin of error of 5 percentage points?
items.explanation: Чтобы погрешность уменьшилась вдвое, √n должен вырасти вдвое, то есть n — вчетверо: 400 (B). 200 — удвоили n; 10 000 — возвели 100 в квадрат.

items.stem: In a random sample of 80 students, the mean time spent on homework was 6.5 hours per week, with a margin of error of 0.8 hour. What is the greatest plausible value for the mean time spent on homework by all students in the population?
items.explanation: Верхняя граница: 6.5 + 0.8 = 7.3 часа.

items.stem: A company randomly selected 500 of its 20,000 customers; 90 of them said they would buy a new product. The margin of error for the percent is 3.4 percentage points. Which is a plausible range for the number of all 20,000 customers who would buy the product?
items.explanation: Доля 90/500 = 18%, интервал 14.6–21.4%. Умножаем на 20 000: 2920–4280 (A). B — погрешность применили к числу 90; C берёт только верхнюю половину; D — неверный пересчёт погрешности.

items.stem: A school surveyed the members of its computer club about whether the school should buy new laptops, and 85% said yes. Which is the best reason the result cannot be generalized to all students at the school?
choices: Members of the computer club are not a random sample of all students.
The sample is too large.
85% is too high to be accurate.
The survey asked a yes-or-no question.
items.explanation: Члены компьютерного клуба больше интересуются ноутбуками — выборка не случайная и смещённая (A). Высокий процент сам по себе не ошибка (C).

items.stem: A random sample of 50 households in a town had a mean water use of 320 liters per day. The town has 8,000 households. Based on the sample, what is the estimated total daily water use of all households in the town, in thousands of liters?
items.explanation: 320 · 8000 = 2 560 000 литров = 2560 тысяч литров.

items.stem: Two independent random samples estimated the mean height of 10-year-olds in a region. Sample A (50 children): 138 centimeters with a margin of error of 2.0 centimeters. Sample B (200 children): 140 centimeters with a margin of error of 1.0 centimeter. Which statement is true?
choices: The intervals overlap, so the samples are consistent, and sample B's estimate is more precise.
The intervals do not overlap, so the samples contradict each other.
Sample A is more precise because its margin of error is larger.
The true mean must be 139 centimeters.
items.explanation: A: 136–140, B: 139–141 — интервалы пересекаются; у B погрешность меньше, оценка точнее (A). Большая погрешность — меньшая точность (C); 139 — лишь одно из правдоподобных значений (D).

items.stem: A random sample of a city's residents found that 12% use public transit daily, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points. A city planner claims that fewer than 1 in 10 residents use public transit daily. Which is the best evaluation of the claim?
choices: The claim is possible but not supported, because the interval from 9% to 15% includes values above and below 10%.
The claim is proven false, because 12% is greater than 10%.
The claim is proven true, because 9% is less than 10%.
The claim cannot be evaluated without knowing the sample size.
items.explanation: Правдоподобные значения 9–15%: есть и ниже 10%, и выше, причём оценка 12% выше. Опровергнуть нельзя, но и подтверждения нет (A). Погрешность уже учитывает размер выборки (D).

items.stem: In a random sample of 640 voters, 336 support a ballot measure. What is the sample proportion of voters who support the measure, written as a decimal?
items.explanation: Доля = число «за» / размер выборки: 336/640 = 0.525.

items.stem: A factory tests a random sample of 200 of the 50,000 batteries in a lot, and 6 of the batteries in the sample are defective. Which is the best estimate of the number of defective batteries in the whole lot?
A researcher wants to estimate the proportion of a town's residents who own a dog. Which method would give the most reliable estimate?
choices: Selecting 400 residents at random from the town's address list and surveying them
Surveying 2,000 people at a dog park
Posting an online survey and using all responses
Surveying every resident on one street
items.explanation: Случайная выборка из всего города (A). В собачьем парке почти все с собаками — смещение; онлайн-опрос — добровольцы; одна улица не похожа на город. Большой размер B не спасает от смещения.

items.stem: An interval of plausible values for a population mean is centered at 54.2 and has a margin of error of 2.6. What is the lower endpoint of the interval?
items.explanation: Нижняя граница = центр − погрешность: 54.2 − 2.6 = 51.6.

items.stem: Based on a random sample, a researcher estimates that 60% of a population agree with a statement, with a margin of error of 5 percentage points. Which statement is correct?
choices: Plausible values for the percent of the population who agree are from 55% to 65%.
Between 55% and 65% of the people in the sample agreed.
The population percent is 60%, and 5% of people were not counted.
If the survey were repeated, exactly 60% would agree.
items.explanation: Интервал описывает правдоподобные значения для совокупности (A). В выборке согласились ровно 60% (B неверно); погрешность — не пропущенные люди (C); повторная выборка даст другое значение (D).
